definitions.gloss: to go bankrupt; to go out of business; to become insolvent
definitions.explanation: For a business or company to fail financially and cease operations due to inability to pay debts.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{去年|きょねん}→去年：00727_kyonen⟧{倒産|とうさん}した。
examples.english: That company went bankrupt last year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{不景気|ふけいき}→不景気：18557_fukeiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}→中小企業：24117_chuushoukigyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{倒産|とうさん}した。
examples.english: Many small and medium-sized businesses went bankrupt due to the recession.

examples.japanese: ⟦{取引先|とりひきさき}→取引先：11083_torihikisaki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{突然|とつぜん}→突然：00409_totsuzen⟧{倒産|とうさん}して、うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{影響|えいきょう}→影響：01877_eikyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。
examples.english: A business partner suddenly went bankrupt, and our company was significantly affected too.

notes:
Used specifically for businesses and companies, not for individuals. An intransitive verb — the company itself is the subject. Frequently appears in news reports about the economy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {倒産件数|とうさんけんすう}: number of bankruptcies
- {連鎖倒産|れんさとうさん}: chain of bankruptcies; domino-effect failures
- ⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる→追い込む：06371_oikomu⟧: to be driven to bankruptcy
- ⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危機|きき}→危機：11798_kiki⟧: risk of bankruptcy
- ⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{免|まぬが}れる→免れる：10548_manugareru⟧: to avoid bankruptcy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{破産|はさん}→破産：03555_hasan⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to go bankrupt — can be used for both individuals and businesses; a broader legal term
- ⟦{廃業|はいぎょう}→廃業：20645_haigyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to close down a business — voluntary closure, not necessarily due to financial failure
- ⟦{潰|つぶ}れる→潰れる：04249_tsubureru⟧: to go under; to collapse — colloquial equivalent of {倒産|とうさん}する
